newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajiks subject U.N. observers to mock execution.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks subject U.N. observers to mock execution.

text.p: United Nations observers monitoring the implementation of a ceasefire in war-torn Tajikistan were subjected to a mock execution by Tajik government troops, the U.N. mission said on Wednesday.

"UNMOT military observers were subjected to blatant physical and verbal abuse (and) ordered to line up for execution," the U.N. observer mission said in a statement issued in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
It said the incident -- the second time this month Tajik government forces have subjected U.N. observers to physical abuse and a mock execution -- took place on Sunday.
The statement said two observer teams were on the road to Garm, around 150 km (100 miles) east of Dushanbe, when they were stopped at a government checkpoint.
Fighting between government troops and Islamist opposition guerrillas near Garm threatened to scupper the fragile ceasefire agreed last week.

The statement said the observer teams were made to stand in a field where government soldiers fired machine guns around them. The soldiers then started firing at an unmarked car on the road and the observers fled in the confusion.
The attack overshadows peace talks scheduled for Thursday in Moscow aimed at ending the bloody four-year civil war in the former Soviet republic, where renewed fighting was reported east of Dushanbe.
Tajik military sources said government troops and guerrillas clashed with rocket-propelled grenades and automatic weapons around Labijar, near Garm, late on Tuesday.

But Davlatali Davlatov, state adviser to Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, told Reuters that Rakhmonov had left for Moscow on Wednesday where he will meet Islamist opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri for the negotiations.

The incident also highlights the risks international agencies run in the conflicts which exploded after the collapse of the Soviet Union -- six foreign Red Cross workers were murdered in Russia's rebel Chechnya region on Tuesday.
The U.N. mission fields 96 military observers in Tajikistan and had its mandate renewed for a further four months last week.
Previous ceasefires have been routinely flouted. A U.N.-sponsored ceasefire collapsed almost as soon as it was reconfirmed by the warring sides last July.

The civil war has killed tens of thousands and displaced many more in the mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China. Bitter regional and clan rivalries underlie the conflict between the Islamist revels and the secular government.
